text:
Samir: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel merge + new quant profiles I'm seeing a consistent drop in prefix/prompt cache warmup on a few high-QPS routes. Canary numbers: first-token cache miss rate up ~15% on average.

Maya: Confirmed on canary dashboards. Route-level warmup hit dropped from ~0.86 -> ~0.69 within 30s windows for prompt-heavy traces. Tail first-token latency up 25-40ms on affected nodes.

Zheng: Quick correlate: fused-attn-v2 + q8h-swapped landed together. I ran a diff of tokenizer callsites and noticed the fused-attn fastpath invokes a micro-optimized tokenizer variant that pads/token-orders differently for vectorized batches. Could be keying divergence.

Elaine: Uploaded a sampled profiler extract and KV key fingerprint counts from the canary run. Histogram shifted — more unique keys in early steps. See snippet: 
```
# canary sample 2025-04-12T03:25Z
route: /v1/generate:prefix
kernel: fused-attn-v2
quant_profile: q8h-swapped
warmup_window_s: 30
prefix_hit_rate_before: 0.86
prefix_hit_rate_after: 0.69
sampled_kv_keys_top:
  - 0x4f2a: 12.3% (was 18.9%)
  - 0x91bb: 9.1% (was 13.4%)
unique_keys_early_pct: 27% (was 12%)
```

Samir: I ran kv_key_inspect on a failing trace — the key pipeline hashed raw token ids, and the tokenizer variant produced a different order/ids for first tokens. That explains the new keys.

deploy-bot: rollout fused-attn-v2 -> prod triggered @ 2025-04-12T03:22Z (canary -> gradual).

Maya: Did a quick A/B: forced old tokenizer function into a canary worker and warmup hit-rate recovered to ~85% in the same window. Reproducible on our test traces.

Zheng: Hypothesis: fused-attn fastpath reorders pad/CLS tokens to optimize register packing; quant grouping might change padding emission for short contexts. Both can alter the token sequence used for prefix keying.

Elaine: Short-term mitigations I'm proposing:
- runtime flag kv_compat_mode=true to canonicalize token stream before keying (CPU-only shim) — cheap to enable as canary
- rollback fused-attn fastpath on affected fleets if warmup doesn't recover within the rollout window

Maya: Medium-term: add a canonicalization API at the kernel boundary so all tokenizer variants normalize to a stable key sequence (normalize, strip pad-order differences, stable-id-map). Also add unit/e2e tests that assert key fingerprint stability across kernel/quant variants.

Samir: Action items:
- @Zheng: prototype kv_compat_mode shim + measure perf delta (ETA 6h)
- @Elaine: file ticket with traces + perf dumps; add canary bump backstop (ETA 1h)
- @Maya: run high-traffic route tests with kv_compat_mode on canary and capture warmup-hit and TTR (ETA 8h)

Zheng: Note: expect small CPU overhead (~2-3% p99) for canonicalization; still cheaper than missed cache token cost. Starting prototype now.

Elaine: I'll update routing for impacted customers and add a console alert rule for >=10% warmup-hit drop on a route during rollout.

Samir: Please post results here. If kv_compat_mode recovers >80% warmup hit we'll keep it and schedule kernel follow-up; otherwise prepare rollback.

ops-bot: alert created: TICKET-4912 "prefix-cache hit drop after fused-attn rollout" (prio=P1) assigned to eng-runtime.

Maya: tl;dr — root cause likely tokenizer output variation introduced by fused kernel fastpath (padding/order). Short fix = key-normalization shim; medium fix = invariants/tests at kernel boundary. :+1:
